guides.favoredWhen: Cage blocks her dashes and your R scales on low HP. Hold cage, stack, one-shot late.

keyTips.text: Your cage blocks her dashes: hold it until she Es.
One stun per cage: she counts it before committing, so vary.
Your R scales on low HP: hold it for the execute.

tips.text: Your Q hits two targets: line her up with the wave.
Her Q-R one-shots late: respect the spike, keep HP.
She trades HP for E2 damage: punish the stun she eats.
She roams to stop your scaling: stack while she shows elsewhere.
Scaled plus caged: the Akali who never stops you never wins.

sources.author: Anguish333
sources.rankClaim: Master (profile badge; title claims 2000LP GrandMaster EUW and Challenger EUNE) · Akali main

guides.favoredWhen: She pushes from level 1, dodges the cage with W, and snowballs before you scale. Stack safe, hold cage.

keyTips.text: She dodges your cage with W speed (about {cd:45:E}): cast it where she lands.
She pushes from level 1: concede the wave, stack the minions.
She punishes your last hits in levels 1-5: you are very weak early, so give CS.

tips.text: She forces the choice: Q her or last-hit; stack first.
She keeps you pinned: you cannot hold the wave, so call the jungler.
After 6 she shoves and roams to snowball: match the shove late, stack under tower.
She coordinates dives with her jungler: a diver plus Charm beats cage from 6 on, so track it.
She ends before your scaling matters: your power only grows, so survive.

sources.author: star zall
sources.rankClaim: Challenger Veigar OTP 3260 LP Peak (title, no badge) · Veigar main

guides.favoredWhen: She abuses your weak trades and waveclear. Stack under tower, hold flash for ganks.

keyTips.text: Very easy for her: your trades and waveclear both lose, so concede.
She pokes every step-up: weak trades mean lost HP, so give ground.
Your cage plus gank, especially with her flash down: that is your only out.

tips.text: She shoves from level 1: your waveclear cannot answer, so stack.
She trades on cooldown: weak trades lose every exchange, so never answer.
Cage plus jungler is the kill setup: call him when her flash is down.
She keeps flash for the cage: no flash means she walks up, so punish.
Farmed plus flash tracked: the Syndra who never answers your cage never stops you.

guides.favoredWhen: He respects the cage, punishes it when down, and dodges your R with his. Hold cage, stack, end it.

keyTips.text: Your cage gates his all-ins: hold it while he looks.
Cage down means he runs you down: the cooldown is his kill signal, so track it.
His R answers your R: never ult a Zed holding Death Mark.

early-lane.text: Zed often places Living Shadow before Death Mark so he can swap away from skillshots. Hold your crowd control until he has used the swap.

win-condition.text: Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.

tips.text: He chips with shadow poke: dodge shadows, stack anyway.
He farms to Voltaic: punish before the spike.
Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.
His Edge of Night second: with it your cage cannot catch him after R, so end it first.
Cage up plus R held: that combination denies the kill every time.

keyTips.text: Play safely through the opening levels; Veigar needs time, gold, and experience before he can carry fights.
Keep Event Horizon available to stop a dive or all-in; it is his only self-peel and has a long cooldown.
After reaching level six, use the full ability kit to set up a finish: poke first, then let Primordial Burst execute the low target.

tips.text: Avoid trades unless the lane has a clear advantage; early pressure depends heavily on the support.
Use Baleful Strike to farm and build passive stacks when doing so is safe.
Use Event Horizon to zone an approach or chain the support's crowd control; its cage also gives the jungler a gank setup.
After taking the bot outer tower, rotate mid and help take that tower to open the map.
Farm a side lane and keep collecting passive stacks before opponents begin grouping.
When the enemy starts grouping, join the team rather than staying isolated.
Look for an Event Horizon catch; after a pick, call for Dragon or Baron while the enemy is down a player.
Level nine maxes the first ability and makes Baleful Strike a meaningful chunk of a squishy target.
Two ultimate points at level eleven sharply improve the follow-up damage after the cage or teammates' crowd control.
Stay with allies in late game so the enemy cannot pick Veigar off or force a four-versus-five.
Use Event Horizon to create a numbers advantage, then Primordial Burst to remove the caught target before taking a nearby objective or sieging.
If ahead, prioritize an accessible squishy with Primordial Burst to remove damage from the fight.
Use choke points to improve the chance that Event Horizon and Dark Matter control the fight; avoid walking alone into fog because Veigar is immobile.

itemization.text: Take First Strike, Magical Footwear, Biscuit Delivery, and Cosmic Insight with Manaflow Band and Transcendence as the 16.21 setup.
Build the popular path of Luden's Echo, Sorcerer's Shoes, Stormsurge, Rabadon's Deathcap, and Zhonya's Hourglass.
Start Doran's Ring, a Health Potion, and Stealth Ward.
Choose Banshee's Veil as the fourth-item alternative to Rabadon's against burst damage or key crowd control.
Max Q, then W, then E, taking Primordial Burst at levels six, eleven, and sixteen.

keyTips.text: Prioritize farm and experience; Veigar is weak early and needs time and gold to come online.
Keep Event Horizon ready to prevent an all-in; do not spend his only self-peel casually.
At level six, use Event Horizon to control space and connect Dark Matter and Baleful Strike, then look for Primordial Burst as the finishing damage.

tips.text: Use Baleful Strike to collect passive stacks when it does not expose Veigar to a bad trade.
Avoid fighting until there is an item advantage or another clear opening.
Against all-in champions, hold Event Horizon through the trade window instead of spending it for poke.
When the enemy bot lane leaves mid after taking its tower, move to a side lane to keep farming and gaining experience.
Side-lane to keep stacking while the map is quiet, then group when the enemy begins grouping.
Use Event Horizon to catch an isolated opponent; turn the pick into Dragon or Baron pressure.
Maxing the first ability by level nine makes Baleful Strike a substantial hit on squishy targets.
Two ultimate points at level eleven increase his ability to finish targets after the team controls them.
Passive stacks add ability power over time, so take safe farm and stacks rather than forcing unnecessary fights.
Stay with the team late; do not walk off alone and give the enemy a four-versus-five opening.
Use Event Horizon to produce a pick, then Primordial Burst to finish the target before the team takes a nearby objective or sieges.
If ahead, use Primordial Burst on an accessible squishy to remove a key damage source.
Use choke points to make Event Horizon catches easier and preserve the cage as a way to secure picks.

itemization.text: Take First Strike, Magical Footwear, Biscuit Delivery, and Cosmic Insight with Manaflow Band and Transcendence as the 16.21 rune page.
Build the popular path of Rod of Ages, Sorcerer's Shoes, Archangel's Staff, Rabadon's Deathcap, and Zhonya's Hourglass.
Start Doran's Ring, a Health Potion, and Stealth Ward.
Choose Shadowflame as the fourth-item alternative to Rabadon's against healing and shielding champions.
Max Q, then W, then E, taking Primordial Burst at levels six, eleven, and sixteen.
